literal: Intense hunger and, unceasing disease and, destructive enmity and, without joining, that which functions [is a] country.
translation: A true country is one that functions without being touched by intense hunger, unceasing disease, and destructive enmity.
modern: கொடிய பசியும், தீராத நோயும், அழிக்கும் பகையும் தன்னிடம் சேராமல் நடைபெறும் நாடே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the ideal state of a nation by listing three major threats it must avoid. Intense hunger points to famine or extreme poverty. Unceasing disease refers to chronic epidemics or poor public health. Destructive enmity indicates external invasions or internal strife. A true country is one that functions and prospers without these three evils ever taking root.
